findings.title: Call to undefined isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() fails compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but no such method exists anywhere in its hierarchy. UsernameForm extends UsernamePasswordForm, which only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:161); AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator define neither. The full contents of all these files at head confirm there is no no-arg variant (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator only has `isPasskeysEnabled()`). This makes the services module fail to compile, so the whole PR cannot build. Either add the no-arg helper (e.g. `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`) or call the correct existing method.

findings.title: Conditional passkey UI no longer set up when no user is identified
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns false whenever `user == null`. It is used in authenticate() (line 115) to decide whether to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm`, and in the error challenge() (lines 137-140). Because the previous `context.getUser() == null` branch that called fillContextForm was removed, on the initial login page (no user selected) and after failures where the user is cleared/unknown, `context.getUser()` is null and fillContextForm is never called. That means the WebAuthn challenge/AUTH_CHALLENGE_NOTE and ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attribute are not placed on the form, so the passkey autofill (`username webauthn` autocomplete, `#webauth` form) disappears from exactly the pages where conditional UI is needed. This regresses existing behavior and contradicts the PR's own assertions that expect `//form[@id='webauth']` on the initial page and after a failed password (e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey line 196 and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey line 211). The gate should depend only on `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`, not on `user != null`.

findings.title: Unused NoSuchElementException import will fail the unused-import check
findings.body: This PR replaces both `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` usages in passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(...), notNullValue())`, so `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` is no longer referenced anywhere in the file. The import remains, which trips Keycloak's checkstyle UnusedImports rule and fails the build. Remove the import.
